page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, providing 1 dedicated physical core configured as 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and provides no discrete GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the small dual-thread physical configuration. In CPU testing, single-threaded throughput shows median capabilities, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1880.19 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1310.0. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics fall into lower percentiles due to the two-vCPU ceiling, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1547.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2986.9. Memory operations show uncached read speeds of 7.6 GB/sec and write speeds of 6.13 GB/sec. Application testing records Redis throughput at 1.99 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput at 2.69 GB/sec, while small 135M language model inference achieves 63.13 generation tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, ecs.g7.large provides a low entry footprint for standard enterprise compute environments. While overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth are limited by the single underlying physical core, its dedicated CPU allocation avoids hypervisor throttling seen in burstable classes. The absence of local disk requires reliant cloud storage volumes for all persistent data. This server profile fits lightweight web servers, background task runners, small microservices, dev-test environments, and low-traffic operational databases that require balanced memory-to-CPU allocations without intensive parallel processing demands.
